records.context: **An unlabelled cell is an abstention, not a disagreement.** Every pair is scored on the rows *both* annotators labelled (pairwise complete cases). Rows where only one of them committed are counted and reported separately as ``n_abstained``. Treating them as disagreements would silently deflate κ in proportion to how far behind the slower annotator is — which is a property of the calendar, not of the annotation.
records.label: spacr.agreement#6
records.source: **An unlabelled cell is an abstention, not a disagreement.** Every pair is scored on the rows *both* annotators labelled (pairwise complete cases). Rows where only one of them committed are counted and reported separately as ``n_abstained``. Treating them as disagreements would silently deflate κ in proportion to how far behind the slower annotator is — which is a property of the calendar, not of the annotation.
records.translation: **Una célula sin etiquetar es una abstención, no un desacuerdo.** Cada par se marca en las filas *ambos anotadores* etiquetados (casos completos por pares). Las filas donde sólo uno de ellos se compromete se cuentan e informan por separado como ``n_abstained``. Tratarlos como desacuerdos desinflaría silenciosamente κ en proporción a lo lejos que está detrás del anotador más lento —que es una propiedad del calendario, no de la anotación.

records.context: :func:`spacr.io._read_and_join_tables` takes six named columns off ``png_list`` -- the object id, ``png_path`` and the four microscope field of view structured-data names -- and drops the rest. The rest is every annotation column the Annotate app added and every score the machine-learning classification model wrote, which for this export are among the most valuable columns in the database: without them ``obs`` has no label to train on, group by, or colour a UMAP with. They are re-attached by object identifier (:func:`_attach_png_labels`) *before* filtering, so a filter can name one -- "export the cells I annotated as infected" -- and they are separated into ``uns['spacr']['annotation_columns']`` and ``uns['spacr']['prediction_columns']`` using :mod:`spacr.agreement`'s own rule, which exists because a model's class column is indistinguishable *by shape* from an annotation pass.
records.label: spacr.anndata_export#28
records.source: :func:`spacr.io._read_and_join_tables` takes six named columns off ``png_list`` -- the object id, ``png_path`` and the four field keys -- and drops the rest. The rest is every annotation column the Annotate app added and every score the classifier wrote, which for this export are among the most valuable columns in the database: without them ``obs`` has no label to train on, group by, or colour a UMAP with. They are re-attached by object key (:func:`_attach_png_labels`) *before* filtering, so a filter can name one -- "export the cells I annotated as infected" -- and they are separated into ``uns['spacr']['annotation_columns']`` and ``uns['spacr']['prediction_columns']`` using :mod:`spacr.agreement`'s own rule, which exists because a model's class column is indistinguishable *by shape* from an annotation pass.
records.translation: :func:`spacr.io._read_and_join_tables` toma seis columnas nombradas de ``png_list`` -- el objeto id, ``png_path`` y los cuatro campos de visión de datos estructurados -- y deja caer el resto. El resto es cada columna de anotación que la aplicación Annotate añadió y cada puntuación que el modelo de clasificación de aprendizaje automático escribió, que para esta exportación se encuentran entre las columnas más valiosas de la base de datos: sin ellos ``obs`` no tiene etiqueta para entrenar, agrupar o colorear un UMAP con. Se vuelven a unir por identificador de objeto (:func:`_attach_png_labels`) *antes* filtrado, por lo que un filtro puede nombrar uno -- "exportar las células que anoté como infectadas" -- y se separan en ``uns['spacr']['annotation_columns']`` y ``uns['spacr']['prediction_columns']`` usando la propia regla de :mod:`spacr.agreement`, que existe porque la columna de clase de un modelo es indistinguible*por forma* de un pase de anotación.

records.context: Increasing the number of cells in a microplate sample position increases the number of possible assignments but does not change the posterior probability for an individual cell. The functions in this module therefore keep annotation coverage and assignment confidence as separate quantities.

records.source: Increasing the number of cells in a well increases the number of possible assignments but does not change the posterior probability for an individual cell. That probability changes when guide fractions or classifier performance change. The functions in this module therefore keep annotation coverage and assignment confidence as separate quantities.
records.translation: El aumento del número de células en una posición de muestra de microplaca aumenta el número de asignaciones posibles, pero no cambia la probabilidad posterior para una célula individual. Esa probabilidad cambia cuando cambian las fracciones guía o el rendimiento del modelo de clasificación de aprendizaje automático. Por lo tanto, las funciones de este módulo mantienen la cobertura de anotación y la confianza de la asignación como cantidades separadas.

records.context: The workflow tunes an embedding on one control subset, evaluates separation on held-out controls, and summarizes each annotated cell by the fraction of nearby controls that are positive. Guide-level purity can then be compared with independently estimated effect signs by permutation testing.
records.label: spacr.annotation_umap_qc#1
records.source: The workflow tunes an embedding on one control subset, evaluates separation on held-out controls, and summarizes each annotated cell by the fraction of nearby controls that are positive. Guide-level purity can then be compared with independently estimated effect signs by permutation testing.
records.translation: El flujo de trabajo sintoniza una incrustación en un subconjunto de control, evalúa la separación en los controles de retención y resume cada célula anotada por la fracción de controles cercanos que son positivos. La pureza del nivel de guía puede entonces compararse con los signos de efecto estimados independientemente mediante pruebas de permutación.

records.translation: Una célula infectada lee 0 y su vecino inmediato lee un paso de píxel, no 0. El campo es cero en cada píxEL infectado y crece hacia el exterior, por lo que una célula que comparte un borde con uno infectado tiene su pixel más cercano a un paso: el mínimo sobre esa célula es 1. Sólo una célula cuyos propios píxeles están infectados lee 0.

records.translation: Una pantalla que no es un módulo de flujo de trabajo — los exploradores de tablas, los espectadores — todavía dice lo que quiere en el vocabulario compartido, y esto es lo que convierte esa palabra en una ruta. La declaración se busca en :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS`: un puerto *producido* primero, porque el módulo que escribe un tipo es el que sabe a dónde va, y un puerto consumido sólo cuando nada lo produce.

records.context: 1. **a pinned value wins.**  If the user has typed a path for this structured-data name, it is restored and is not overwritten by a newer upstream run, a different plate or a restart.  When the upstream has moved since, the move is reported in :attr:`Resolution.held` for an interface to *offer*; 2. otherwise, a value already in ``settings`` that is not a placeholder wins.  Loading a settings CSV, dropping a folder or seeding from another screen all land here, and none of them is overridden within the same session; 3. otherwise the registry's answer is used.
records.label: spacr.chaining.resolve_settings#2
records.source: 1. **a pinned value wins.**  If the user has typed a path for this key, it is restored and is not overwritten by a newer upstream run, a different plate or a restart.  When the upstream has moved since, the move is reported in :attr:`Resolution.held` for an interface to *offer*; 2. otherwise, a value already in ``settings`` that is not a placeholder wins.  Loading a settings CSV, dropping a folder or seeding from another screen all land here, and none of them is overridden within the same session; 3. otherwise the registry's answer is used.
records.translation: 1. Gana el valor fijado **a.** Si el usuario ha tecleado una ruta para este nombre de datos estructurados, se restablece y no se sobreescribe mediante una ejecución ascendente más reciente, una placa diferente o un reinicio. Cuando el paso ascendente se ha movido desde entonces, el movimiento se reporta en :attr:`Resolution.held` para una interfaz a *offer*; 2. de lo contrario, gana un valor ya en ``settings`` que no es un marcador de posición. Cargando una configuración CSV, soltando una carpeta o sembrando desde otra pantalla todo el terreno aquí, y ninguno de ellos se sobrepone dentro de la misma sesión; 3. de otro modo se utiliza la respuesta del registro.

records.context: Planning and loading are separate. :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand extracted image regions, so a screen can execute it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that executes the second half on a background execution unit gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.label: spacr.crop_loader#2
records.source: Planning and loading are separate. :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand crops, so a screen can run it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that runs the second half on a worker thread gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.translation: La planificación y la carga son separadas. :func:`plan_crops` pregunta a la base de datos o a la carpeta *qué objetos coinciden con* y no lee píxeles en absoluto: un ``COUNT`` y un ``SELECT`` de identificadores, o un ``scandir``. Es milisegundos en una placa de sesenta mil regiones de imágenes extraídas, por lo que una pantalla puede ejecutarlo en un clic y decirle al usuario lo que pidió antes de comprometerse a leer cualquiera de ellos. :func:`load_crops` luego lee los píxeles en páginas, informando después de cada una. Un llamante que ejecuta la segunda mitad en una unidad de ejecución de fondo obtiene un número de progreso por página y una parada que tiene efecto dentro de una página en lugar de al final.

records.context: **Bounding box versus object.** A bounding box is the smallest rectangle containing the object; an object-image-region masks everything outside it away. Both are useful -- the background around a cell is sometimes signal and sometimes contamination -- so it is a setting. Database-sourced objects can only ever be bounding boxes: a coordinate has no outline to mask against.

records.source: **Bounding box versus object.** A bounding box is the smallest rectangle containing the object; an object crop masks everything outside it away. records.translation: Un cuadro delimitador es el rectángulo más pequeño que contiene el objeto; **Caja delimitadora versus objeto.** Un objeto-imagen-región enmascara todo lo que está fuera de ella. Los objetos de origen de base de datos solo pueden ser cuadros delimitadores: una coordenada no tiene un contorno contra el que enmascararse.

records.context: 4 or more: **refused**. cv2 would write BGRA, and PIL then reads the fourth intensity image layer as an alpha image data channel and drops it on ``convert('RGB')`` -- a whole stain silently deleted from every extracted image region. ``settings['png_dims']`` documents a maximum of three entries; this is where a fourth stops being ignored and starts being an error.
records.label: spacr.crops.to_cv2_bgr#5
records.source: 4 or more: **refused**. cv2 would write BGRA, and PIL then reads the fourth intensity plane as an alpha channel and drops it on ``convert('RGB')`` -- a whole stain silently deleted from every crop. ``settings['png_dims']`` documents a maximum of three entries; this is where a fourth stops being ignored and starts being an error.
records.translation: 4 o más: **refused**. cv2 escribiría BGRA, y PIL entonces leería la cuarta capa de imagen de intensidad como un canal de datos de imagen alfa y lo soltaría en ``convert('RGB')`` -- una tinción entera borrada silenciosamente de cada región de imagen extraída. ``settings['png_dims']`` documenta un máximo de tres entradas; aquí es donde una cuarta deja de ser ignorada y comienza a ser un error.

records.context: **Track correction.** A btrack track breaks when a cell divides or briefly leaves focus, and two tracks get swapped when cells touch. A velocity computed over a track that follows two cells is wrong, not merely noisy. :class:`TrackCuration` joins, splits and deletes tracks.
records.label: spacr.curation#3
records.source: **Track correction.** A btrack track breaks when a cell divides or briefly leaves focus, and two tracks get swapped when cells touch. A velocity computed over a track that follows two cells is wrong, not merely noisy. :class:`TrackCuration` joins, splits and deletes tracks.
records.translation: **Corrección de la secuencia.** Una pista btrack se rompe cuando una célula se divide o deja brevemente el foco, y dos pistas se intercambian cuando las células tocan. Una velocidad calculada sobre una pista que sigue dos células es incorrecta, no simplemente ruidosa. :class:`TrackCuration` une, divide y elimina pistas.

records.context: The other half of the commonest pair of errors: two cells touch, the tracker swaps them, and one id follows cell A then cell B. Splitting at the frame where it changed hands turns one wrong track into two right ones.
records.label: spacr.curation.TrackCuration.split#1
records.source: The other half of the commonest pair of errors: two cells touch, the tracker swaps them, and one id follows cell A then cell B. Splitting at the frame where it changed hands turns one wrong track into two right ones.
records.translation: La otra mitad del par de errores más común: dos células tocan, el rastreador las intercambia, y un identificador sigue la célula A y luego la célula B. Dividir en el marco donde cambió de manos convierte una pista equivocada en dos rectas correctas.

records.source: :class:`spacr.qt.prerun.DiameterPanel` sits above the Run row on the Mask screen: it reads the channels off the settings form with :func:`channels_from_settings`, calls :func:`estimate_diameters` on a worker thread, and shows one row per object type carrying the proposal *and its evidence* — the 10th-90th percentile range, how many objects it was pooled from, how many fields contributed, the method and the confidence. Nothing is written into ``<object>_diameter`` until the user presses **Use**, and :attr:`DiameterEstimate.usable` is checked first, so the NaN an unmeasurable channel returns cannot reach a settings field.
records.translation: :class:`spacr.qt.prerun.DiameterPanel` se encuentra por encima de la fila de sesión de procesamiento en la vista de la aplicación Mask: lee los canales de datos de imagen fuera del formulario de configuración con :func:`channels_from_settings`, llama a :func:`estimate_diameters` en una unidad de ejecución de fondo, y muestra una fila por tipo de objeto que lleva la propuesta *y su evidencia* — el rango de percentil 10o-90, cuántos objetos fue agrupado, cuántos campos de visión del microscopio contribuyeron, el método y la confianza. Nada se escribe en ``<object>_diameter`` hasta que el usuario presiona **Use**, y :attr:`DiameterEstimate.usable` se comprueba primero, por lo que el canal de datos NaN no puede llegar a un campo de configuración.

records.context: The workflow passes the response as one row per guide-in-well, but the response is a property of the well -- on the reference screen `log_pred` has exactly one distinct value in each of the 610 microplate sample positions, repeated once per guide the well retained. Counting every row would count a 15-guide well fifteen times and give n = 1,945 for 610 independent observations, overstating the evidence three-fold and weighting the distribution towards microplate sample positions with many guides.
records.label: spacr.figures.distributions.one_value_per_well#2
records.source: The pipeline passes the response as one row per guide-in-well, but the response is a property of the well -- on the reference screen `log_pred` has exactly one distinct value in each of the 610 wells, repeated once per guide the well retained. Counting every row would count a 15-guide well fifteen times and give n = 1,945 for 610 independent observations, overstating the evidence three-fold and weighting the distribution towards wells with many guides.
records.translation: El flujo de trabajo pasa la respuesta como una fila por guía-en-well, pero la respuesta es una propiedad del pozo -- en la cribado de referencia `log_pred` tiene exactamente un valor distinto en cada una de las 610 posiciones de la muestra de microplaca, repetido una vez por guía el pozo retenido. Contar cada fila contaría un pozo de 15 guías quince veces y dar n = 1.945 para 610 observaciones independientes, exagerando la evidencia tres veces y ponderando la distribución hacia posiciones de muestra de Microplaca con muchas guías.

records.context: The raw fraction confounds evenness with how many guides were retained in the well: a two-guide well and a fifteen-guide well produce shares an order of magnitude apart with no unevenness at all. Dividing by the well's own equal share removes that dependence, so a single reference line at 1 applies to every well.
records.label: spacr.figures.distributions.relative_representation#2
records.source: The raw fraction confounds evenness with how many guides were retained in the well: a two-guide well and a fifteen-guide well produce shares an order of magnitude apart with no unevenness at all. Dividing by the well's own equal share removes that dependence, so a single reference line at 1 applies to every well.
records.translation: La fracción cruda confunde la uniformidad con la cantidad de guías retenidas en el pozo: un pozo de dos guías y un pozo de quince guías producen proporciones un orden de magnitud aparte sin ninguna desigualdad en absoluto. Dividir por la propia parte igual del pozo elimina esa dependencia, por lo que una sola línea de referencia en 1 se aplica a cada pozo.

records.context: which kind of object ``frame`` holds -- the name of the measurement table it was read from. Pass it whenever it is known. ``filters`` holds cells, nuclei and pathogens side by side, and ``object_label`` is unique within a microscope field of view only for ONE kind: a merge that leaves the type out writes a data-selection boundary drawn on nucleus 2 onto cell 2 as well, which is the same wrong answer :func:`require_full_identity` exists to prevent, one axis over. ``None`` keeps the type-blind merge for a caller that genuinely cannot say, and for a database with no ``object_type`` column.
records.label: spacr.filters.export_gate#6
records.source: which kind of object ``frame`` holds -- the name of the measurement table it was read from. Pass it whenever it is known. ``filters`` holds cells, nuclei and pathogens side by side, and ``object_label`` is unique within a field only for ONE kind: a merge that leaves the type out writes a gate drawn on nucleus 2 onto cell 2 as well, which is the same wrong answer :func:`require_full_identity` exists to prevent, one axis over. ``None`` keeps the type-blind merge for a caller that genuinely cannot say, and for a database with no ``object_type`` column.
records.translation: que tipo de objeto ``frame`` contiene -- el nombre de la tabla de medición de la que se leyó. Pásala siempre que se sepa. ``filters`` contiene células, núcleos y patógenos uno al lado del otro, y ``object_label`` es único dentro de un campo de visión del microscopio sólo para un tipo: una fusión que deja el tipo hacia fuera escribe un límite de selección de datos dibujado en el núcleo 2 en la célula 2 también, que es la misma respuesta incorrecta :func:`require_full_identity` existe para prevenir, Un eje más. ``None`` mantiene la fusión tipo ciego para un llamante que realmente no puede decir, y para una base de datos sin columna ``object_type``.

records.context: This is a merge onto the canonical structured-data names rather than a substitution for them because the canonical tables carry things a foreign table cannot reproduce: every spaCR feature column, and ``cell_id``, the link from a nucleus or pathogen back to the cell that contains it. Replacing the table would drop both, and a parent-child link is not recoverable from what is left. ``conversion_map`` gets the same treatment — merged on the output filename, never replaced — so a project's provenance back to its own original files survives an import into it.
records.label: spacr.foreign#13
records.source: This is a merge onto the canonical keys rather than a substitution for them because the canonical tables carry things a foreign table cannot reproduce: every spaCR feature column, and ``cell_id``, the link from a nucleus or pathogen back to the cell that contains it. Replacing the table would drop both, and a parent-child link is not recoverable from what is left. ``conversion_map`` gets the same treatment — merged on the output filename, never replaced — so a project's provenance back to its own original files survives an import into it.
records.translation: Esto es una fusión en los nombres canónicos de datos estructurados en lugar de una sustitución para ellos porque las tablas canónicas llevan cosas que una tabla extraña no puede reproducir: cada columna de características spaCR, y ``cell_id``, el enlace de un núcleo o patógeno de vuelta a la célula que la contiene. Reemplazar la tabla caería tanto, y un enlace padre-hijo no es recuperable de lo que queda. ``conversion_map`` recibe el mismo tratamiento — fusionado en el nombre del archivo de salida, nunca reemplazado — por lo que la procedencia de un proyecto de nuevo a sus propios archivos originales sobrevive una importación en él.

records.source: All values come from :mod:`spacr.annotation` -- the same join that writes the annotated exports -- so the tile and the exported CSV report the same values (for example GRA14's compartment). records.translation: Todos los valores provienen de :mod:`spacr.annotation` -- la misma unión que escribe las exportaciones anotadas -- por lo que el mosaico y el CSV exportados reportan los mismos valores (por ejemplo, el compartimento de GRA14). Este módulo no lee ningún archivo, analiza ningún gen id y no posee ninguna tabla; agrupa las 23 columnas :func:`spacr.annotation.annotate` en orden de lectura y añade las coordenadas por segmento DeepTMHMM que ``annotate`` deja fuera de un coeficiente de exportación.

records.context: Without it, two guides with effects in the same direction would both claim the same top-scoring cells. With it, the total mass attributed to each guide is pinned to its read fraction, so they split the top cells in proportion instead. It is enforced by iterative proportional fitting, which is the same fixed point as fitting a mixture whose mixing proportions are known and fixed.

records.source: Without it, two guides with effects in the same direction would both claim the same top-scoring cells. With it, the total mass attributed to each guide is pinned to its read fraction, so they split the top cells in proportion instead. It is enforced by iterative proportional fitting, which is the same fixed point as fitting a mixture whose mixing proportions are known and fixed.

Con ella, la masa total atribuida a cada guía se fija a su fracción de lectura, por lo que se dividen las células superiores en proporción. Se aplica mediante ajuste proporcional iterativo, que es el mismo punto fijo que instalar una mezcla cuyas proporciones de mezcla son conocidas y fijas.

records.context: Let ``n`` be the number of microplate sample positions and ``G`` the number of guides. A rank-deficient ``Z`` raises ``ValueError`` rather than being pseudo-inverted, because a nuisance basis that cannot be inverted is a design question, not a numerical one.
records.label: spacr.guide_permutation.guide_freedman_lane_test#2
records.source: Let ``n`` be the number of wells and ``G`` the number of guides. For well ``i``, ``y_i`` is the phenotype and ``x_ig`` is guide ``g``'s read fraction. ``Z`` is the ``n x q`` nuisance design: indicator columns for the block (normally ``plateID``) and for each column in ``nuisance_columns`` (normally ``rowID`` and ``columnID``). A rank-deficient ``Z`` raises ``ValueError`` rather than being pseudo-inverted, because a nuisance basis that cannot be inverted is a design question, not a numerical one.
records.translation: Deja que ``n`` sea el número de posiciones de muestra de microplaca y ``G`` el número del guía. Para el pocillo ``i``, ``y_i`` es el fenotipo y ``x_ig`` es la fracción de lectura de la guía ``g``. ``Z`` es el diseño de molestia ``n x q``: columnas indicadoras para el bloque (normalmente ``plateID``) y para cada columna en ``nuisance_columns`` (normalmente ``rowID`` y ``columnID``). Un rango deficiente ``Z`` eleva ``ValueError`` en lugar de ser pseudo-invertido, porque una base de molestia que no se puede invertir es una pregunta de diseño, no numérica.

records.context: This module builds a report from existing tables and runs no image processing: thirteen of the sixteen candidate infection metrics can be derived from tables Measure has already written. The three that do not -- intracellular fraction, vacuoles per cell, distance to the host boundary -- belong to the invasion module and to segmentation, and are deliberately absent here rather than approximated.
records.label: spacr.infection#1
records.source: This module builds a report from existing tables and runs no image processing: thirteen of the sixteen candidate infection metrics can be derived from tables Measure has already written. The three that do not -- intracellular fraction, vacuoles per cell, distance to the host boundary -- belong to the invasion module and to segmentation, and are deliberately absent here rather than approximated.
records.translation: Este módulo construye un informe a partir de tablas existentes y no ejecuta procesamiento de imágenes: trece de las dieciséis métricas de infección candidatas pueden derivarse de tablas ya escritas. Los tres que no -- fracción intracelular, vacuolas por célula, distancia al límite del huésped -- pertenecen al módulo de invasión y a la segmentación, y están deliberadamente ausentes aquí en lugar de aproximarse.

records.context: The relationship table has no row for a cell with no parasites. ``measure.get_components`` explodes the per-cell child list and drops the empty ones, so counting rows there counts infected cells, not all cells. The denominator has to come from the ``cell`` table, which holds every segmented cell whether or not anything is inside it.
records.label: spacr.infection#3
records.source: The relationship table has no row for a cell with no parasites. ``measure.get_components`` explodes the per-cell child list and drops the empty ones, so counting rows there counts infected cells, not all cells. The denominator has to come from the ``cell`` table, which holds every segmented cell whether or not anything is inside it.
records.translation: La tabla de relaciones no tiene fila para una célula sin parásitos. ``measure.get_components`` explota la lista de hijos por célula y deja caer las filas vacías, por lo que contar filas allí cuenta células infectadas, no todas las células. El denominador tiene que venir de la tabla ``cell``, que contiene cada célula segmentada, independientemente de si hay o no algo dentro de ella.

records.translation: El numerador y el denominador deben usar la misma regla de borde; de lo contrario la tasa se calcula contra un conteo de células diferente al numerador.

records.context: The answer determines what the cell table holds. `include_uninfected=False` -- the default for a screen that only extracted image regions infected cells, and what the TSG101 laboratory microplates were measured with -- means Measure wrote no row for a cell with no parasite. The cell table is then a selection of infected cells rather than the segmented population, and `infected / cells` is 1.0 for every microplate sample position no matter what the biology did.
records.label: spacr.infection.uninfected_cells_were_measured#1
records.source: The answer determines what the cell table holds. `include_uninfected=False` -- the default for a screen that only crops infected cells, and what the TSG101 plates were measured with -- means Measure wrote no row for a cell with no parasite. The cell table is then a selection of infected cells rather than the segmented population, and `infected / cells` is 1.0 for every well no matter what the biology did.
records.translation: La respuesta determina lo que contiene la tabla de células. `include_uninfected=False` -- el valor predeterminado para una cribado que sólo extrajo las regiones de imagen infectadas, y con lo que se midieron las microplacas de laboratorio TSG101 -- significa que Measure no escribió ninguna fila para una célula sin parásito. La tabla de células es entonces una selección de células infectadas en lugar de la población segmentada, y `infected / cells` es 1.0 para cada posición de muestra de microplaca no importa lo que la biología hizo.

records.translation: La célula una región de imagen extraída del núcleo pertenece a *is* en el nombre del archivo de la región de la imagen extraida -- :func:`spacr.utils._generate_names` escribe ``<field>_<cell>_<nucleus>.png`` -- pero no se almacena: :func:`spacr.utils.filepaths_to_database` guarda sólo el último token. records.context: The dataset under ``src/<mode>`` is read once and then re-split k ways, so every extracted image region is used for validation exactly once. Folds are class-stratified and, by default, grouped by well so that extracted image regions from the same well stay on one side of the split. records.source: The dataset under ``src/<mode>`` is read once and then re-split k ways, so every crop is used for validation exactly once. Folds are class-stratified and, by default, grouped by well so that crops from the same well stay on one side of the split. Class balancing is applied to the fold's train loader only.
records.translation: El conjunto de datos bajo ``src/<mode>`` se lee una vez y luego se re-divide k maneras, por lo que cada región de imagen extraída se utiliza para la validación exactamente una vez. Los pliegues están estratificados por clase y, por defecto, agrupados por pozo para que las regiones de imagen extraídas del mismo pozo permanezcan en un lado de la división. El balanceo de clase se aplica únicamente a el cargador de entrenamiento del pliegue.

records.context: Every index lands in exactly one validation fold, so the k folds partition the dataset. With ``groups`` supplied, a whole group is assigned to a single fold — extracted image regions from the same well never straddle the train/val line — and groups are placed greedily into whichever fold currently leaves the per-class proportions most even, which is how stratification survives grouping.
records.label: spacr.io.make_cv_folds#1
records.source: Every index lands in exactly one validation fold, so the k folds partition the dataset. With ``groups`` supplied, a whole group is assigned to a single fold — crops from the same well never straddle the train/val line — and groups are placed greedily into whichever fold currently leaves the per-class proportions most even, which is how stratification survives grouping.
records.translation: Cada índice cae exactamente en un pliegue de validación, por lo que la partición k se pliega el conjunto de datos. Con ``groups`` suministrado, un grupo entero se asigna a un solo pliegue — regiones de imagen extraídas del mismo pocillo nunca escalonan la línea entrenamiento/val — y los grupos se colocan codiciosamente en cualquier pliegue que actualmente deja las proporciones por clase más uniforme, que es cómo la estratificación sobrevive a la agrupación.

records.context: Axes are named rather than positional, so two layers with different dimensionality agree on what "z" means; this lets a 2D mask be drawn over a 3D stack.
records.label: spacr.layers.Layer.axes#1
records.source: Axes are named rather than positional, so two layers with different dimensionality agree on what "z" means; this lets a 2D mask be drawn over a 3D stack.
records.translation: Los ejes se denominan en lugar de posicionales, por lo que dos capas con diferente dimensión coinciden en lo que "z" significa; esto permite dibujar una máscara 2D sobre una pila 3D.

records.context: **Every panel uses one world-units-per-pixel scale.** That is the whole difficulty, and it is why this is a class rather than three :meth:`Canvas.covering` calls. Confocal stacks in this codebase are routinely 0.65 µm in xy and 2 µm in z; a side view drawn one pixel per slice is three times too thin, and it does not look wrong — it looks like a slightly flat cell. Nuclear sphericity, colocalisation depth and every 3-D shape feature read off such a picture are wrong by a factor nobody sees. Here the side views are :math:`z_{span}/step` pixels tall, so a 10-slice 2 µm stack is 31 px of a 0.65 µm/px view, not 10.
records.label: spacr.layers.OrthoViews#5
records.source: **Every panel uses one world-units-per-pixel scale.** That is the whole difficulty, and it is why this is a class rather than three :meth:`Canvas.covering` calls. Confocal stacks in this codebase are routinely 0.65 µm in xy and 2 µm in z; a side view drawn one pixel per slice is three times too thin, and it does not look wrong — it looks like a slightly flat cell. Nuclear sphericity, colocalisation depth and every 3-D shape feature read off such a picture are wrong by a factor nobody sees. Here the side views are :math:`z_{span}/step` pixels tall, so a 10-slice 2 µm stack is 31 px of a 0.65 µm/px view, not 10.
records.translation: **Cada panel utiliza una escala mundial de unidades por píxel.** Esa es toda la dificultad, y es la razón por la que esta es una clase en lugar de tres llamadas :meth:`Canvas.covering`. Las pilas de confocal en esta base de código son rutinariamente 0.65 µm en xy y 2 µm en z; una vista lateral dibujada un pixel por rebanada es tres veces demasiado delgada, y no se ve mal — parece una célula ligeramente plana. Esfericidad nuclear, profundidad de colocalización y cada característica de forma 3D leído tal imagen están equivocados por un factor que nadie ve. Aquí las vistas laterales son :math:`z_{span}/step` píxeles de altura, así que una pila de 10 cortes 2 µm es 31 px de una vista 0.55 µm/px, no 10.

records.context: Axes the mapping does not mention are taken to be 0 in world units, which is what a 2-D click on a 3-D layer means once the viewer has supplied the slice it is showing.

records.source: Axes the mapping does not mention are taken to be 0 in world units, which is what a 2-D click on a 3-D layer means once the viewer has supplied the slice it is showing.
records.translation: Los ejes que la asignación no menciona se toman como 0 en unidades del mundo, que es lo que un clic 2D en una capa 3D significa una vez que el espectador ha suministrado la rebanada que se muestra.

records.context: Every object table in ``measurements.db`` is flat, and the relationships between them are already stored: :mod:`spacr.schema` gives ``nucleus`` and ``pathogen`` a ``cell_id`` pointing at the cell they sit inside (:data:`spacr.schema.CHILD_OBJECT_TABLES`). This module assembles those links into a tree, so a question such as "cell 41 in field 3 has one nucleus and four pathogens, and one of those pathogens has an area that would be impossible inside that nucleus" can be answered by inspecting one cell.
records.label: spacr.lineage#1
records.source: Every object table in ``measurements.db`` is flat, and the relationships between them are already stored: :mod:`spacr.schema` gives ``nucleus`` and ``pathogen`` a ``cell_id`` pointing at the cell they sit inside (:data:`spacr.schema.CHILD_OBJECT_TABLES`). This module assembles those links into a tree, so a question such as "cell 41 in field 3 has one nucleus and four pathogens, and one of those pathogens has an area that would be impossible inside that nucleus" can be answered by inspecting one cell.

Este módulo ensambla esos enlaces en un árbol, por lo que una pregunta como "la célula 41 en el campo 3 tiene un núcleo y cuatro patógenos, y uno de esos patógenos tiene un área que sería imposible dentro de ese núcleo" se puede responder inspeccionando una célula.

records.context: **As long as the subtree**, now that the shared key carries the object type. It used not to be: a nucleus 1 and a pathogen 1 inside the same cell were one key, de-duplicating was required (sending the same key twice would draw the same extracted image region twice), and four objects opened as three. :meth:`key_collisions` is the check that this no longer happens — it returns nothing on a typed forest.

The ranking that turns ``C1``/``C2`` into columns 0 and 1 is a property of a set of tokens, and a user fills this table one microscope field of view at a time, so without the stored tokens the second drop would rank its own files from scratch and put ``C2`` in column 0 beside the first drop's ``C1``. records.translation: qué token de canal posee qué columna de canal, por posición: ``channel_tokens[i]`` es el token que la columna ``i`` significa. La mesa almacena esto porque se llena sobre varias gotas. El ranking que convierte ``C1``/``C2`` en columnas 0 y 1 es una propiedad de un conjunto de tokens, y un usuario llena esta tabla un campo a la vez, por lo que sin los tokenes almacenados la segunda gota alinearía sus propios archivos desde cero y pondría ``C2`` en la columna 0 junto a la ``C1`` de la primera gota. Vacío significa que ninguna columna significa ningún token en particular todavía -- cada celda fue llenada por navegación en lugar de por el regex.

records.context: spaCR's ``merged/`` arrays store the image data channels first and then one integer label-mask slice per object class (cell, nucleus, pathogen, organelle). The measurements database records, for every object, its integer ``object_label``, the merged ``.npy`` it came from (``path_name``), its well/microscope field of view metadata, and its features (e.g. ``cell_area``). This function queries that database for the objects you want, then for each hit slices the object out of its array using ``object_label`` and the class mask, assembles the image data channels you ask for into an image, and saves a PNG.
records.label: spacr.measure.generate_object_dataset#1
records.source: spaCR's ``merged/`` arrays store the image channels first and then one integer label-mask slice per object class (cell, nucleus, pathogen, organelle). The measurements database records, for every object, its integer ``object_label``, the merged ``.npy`` it came from (``path_name``), its well/field metadata, and its features (e.g. ``cell_area``). This function queries that database for the objects you want, then for each hit slices the object out of its array using ``object_label`` and the class mask, assembles the channels you ask for into an image, and saves a PNG.
records.translation: Los arrays ``merged/`` de spaCR almacenan los canales de datos de imagen primero y luego un corte entero de etiqueta-máscara por clase de objeto (célula, núcleo, patógeno, orgánulo). La base de datos mide, para cada objeto, su entero ``object_label``, el ``.npy`` fusionado que vino de (``path_name``), sus metadatos de pocillo/campo, y sus características (por ejemplo, ``cell_area``). Esta función consulta esa base de datos para los objetos que desea, luego para cada golpe corta el objeto de su matriz usando ``object_label`` y la máscara de clase, ensambla los canales que pide en una imagen, y guarda un PNG.

records.context: A per-well positive count is not comparable between microplate sample positions of different size: ``process_scores`` sums the response for the count models, so a well of 2000 cells contributes roughly four times the count of a well of 500 at the identical underlying rate. Modelling that count without ``offset(log(Ntotal))`` asks the covariates to explain well size, and any covariate correlated with it comes back as a hit. Measured on a 400-well simulation with a nuisance covariate that drives well size and nothing else, and a true rate coefficient of +1.5: without the offset the nuisance term came back at +1.88 with p = 0, ahead of the real effect; with it, +0.002 with p = 0.90.
records.label: spacr.ml.regression_model._poisson_offset#1
records.source: A per-well positive count is not comparable between wells of different size: ``process_scores`` sums the response for the count models, so a well of 2000 cells contributes roughly four times the count of a well of 500 at the identical underlying rate. Modelling that count without ``offset(log(Ntotal))`` asks the covariates to explain well size, and any covariate correlated with it comes back as a hit. Measured on a 400-well simulation with a nuisance covariate that drives well size and nothing else, and a true rate coefficient of +1.5: without the offset the nuisance term came back at +1.88 with p = 0, ahead of the real effect; with it, +0.002 with p = 0.90.
records.translation: Un conteo positivo por pozo no es comparable entre posiciones de muestra microplaca de diferente tamaño: ``process_scores`` suma la respuesta para los modelos de conteo, por lo que un pozo de 2000 células contribuye aproximadamente cuatro veces el conteo de un pocillo de 500 a la velocidad subyacente idéntica. Modelado que cuenta sin ``offset(log(Ntotal))`` pide a las covariables que expliquen el tamaño del pozo, y cualquier covariable correlacionado con él vuelve como un acierto. Medido en una simulación de 400 pozos con una covariada molestia que determina el tamaño del pocillo y nada más, y un verdadero coeficiente de tasa de +1,5: sin el desplazamiento el término molestia volvió a +1,88 con p = 0, por delante del efecto real; con él, +0,002 con p=0,90.

records.translation: Un cabezal es un modelo de clasificación de aprendizaje automático entrenado: se entrega un lote de regiones de imagen extraídas y devuelve una clase y una probabilidad para cada una. Es un protocolo en lugar de una clase base, por lo que un adaptador alrededor de un módulo torch o un estimador scikit-learn puede suministrarlo. Se planifican dos aplicaciones -- parásitos por vacuole, y lo que es cada objeto -- y el PV uno es tres cabezas en la práctica, entrenado en Hoechst, la tinción de parásitos y CellMask por separado, así que una placa cuenta con cualquier tinción que tenga.

records.context: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-d ngff image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the image data channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#10
records.source: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-D NGFF image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.
records.translation: **1. El espacio está construido a partir de los ejes ESPACIO solamente.** Una imagen 5-d ngff tiene ejes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: el eje de tiempo es en segundos, el eje del canal de datos de imagen no tiene unidad en absoluto, y z/y/x están en micrómetros. Un solo ``Spacing`` sobre los cinco tendría que responder "¿qué unidad es esta?" con una cadena, y lo que sea que respondió sería incorrecto para tres de los ejes — una pila cuyo espacio reclama ``"um"`` mientras que uno de sus ejes pasos en segundos pasa la comprobación de unidad en ``layers.py`` y luego se dibuja a la escala incorrecta. Así que :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` cubre z/Y/X, y t y c se reportan junto con los registros :class:`Axis` a través de :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` y :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nada se pierde; el lector no trata los segundos ni los micrómetros como el mismo tipo de número.

records.context: The writer builds a pyramid by **2x block mean over the two fastest-varying space axes** (see :func:`write_ome_zarr`). It is a box filter and **not a Gaussian pyramid**: there is no pre-filter beyond the box, so it aliases where a properly filtered pyramid would not. It is chosen anyway because it is separable, exact, dependency-free, and the same ``local_mean`` the rest of the NGFF ecosystem writes — matching what other viewers produce matters more here than a marginally better kernel. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#18
records.source: The writer builds a pyramid by **2x block mean over the two fastest-varying space axes** (see :func:`write_ome_zarr`). It is a box filter and **not a Gaussian pyramid**: there is no pre-filter beyond the box, so it aliases where a properly filtered pyramid would not. It is chosen anyway because it is separable, exact, dependency-free, and the same ``local_mean`` the rest of the NGFF ecosystem writes — matching what other viewers produce matters more here than a marginally better kernel. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.
records.translation: El escritor construye una pirámide por bloque **2x media sobre los dos ejes espaciales más rápidos** (ver :func:`write_ome_zarr`). Es un filtro de caja y **no una pirámide gaussiana**: no hay prefiltro más allá de la caja, por lo que alias donde una pirámide correctamente filtrada no lo haría. Se elige de todos modos porque es separable, exacta, libre de dependencia, y el mismo ``local_mean`` el resto del ecosistema NGFF escribe — emparejando lo que otros espectadores producen importa más aquí que un núcleo marginalmente mejor. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) se ofrece y es **mandatory para matrices de etiquetas/máscaras**: la media de las etiquetas 3 y 5 es 4, un objeto que no existe.

records.translation: Un ciclo es rechazado. Un código de barras es una secuencia a través de ciclos; un único "cycle" que llega aquí es bien una ejecución que perdió su eje de ciclo o un llamante que lo colapsó. Ambos producen un código de barra decodificable de ruido, y ninguno es visible aguas abajo. Si un experimento de un solo ciclo necesita alguna vez decodificación debe decir explícitamente en lugar de llegar luciendo como este error.

records.context: A cell contains several spots and they will not all decode identically: an out-of-focus spot, a spot shared with a neighbour, and a genuine second perturbation all look the same at this stage. So a cell is assigned only when its reads AGREE -- ``min_fraction`` of at least ``min_reads`` must carry the same barcode -- and is otherwise left unassigned.
records.label: spacr.ops_sbs.assign_reads_to_cells#1
records.source: A cell contains several spots and they will not all decode identically: an out-of-focus spot, a spot shared with a neighbour, and a genuine second perturbation all look the same at this stage. So a cell is assigned only when its reads AGREE -- ``min_fraction`` of at least ``min_reads`` must carry the same barcode -- and is otherwise left unassigned.
records.translation: Una célula contiene varios puntos y no todos decodifican idénticamente: un punto fuera de foco, un punto compartido con un vecino, y una segunda perturbación genuina todos se ven iguales en esta etapa. Así que una célula se asigna sólo cuando sus lecturas AGREE -- ``min_fraction`` de al menos ``min_reads`` debe llevar el mismo código de barras -- y de lo contrario se deja sin firmar.

records.context: The defaults (``min_reads=2``, ``min_fraction=0.6``) are conservative. A single read cannot be checked against anything, and a single mis-called base would silently hand a cell the wrong perturbation. A cell with no barcode costs statistical detection sensitivity; a cell with the WRONG barcode moves a real phenotype onto another guide's average and is not recoverable downstream, because nothing later can tell it happened.
records.label: spacr.ops_sbs.assign_reads_to_cells#2
records.source: The defaults (``min_reads=2``, ``min_fraction=0.6``) are conservative. A single read cannot be checked against anything, and a single mis-called base would silently hand a cell the wrong perturbation. A cell with no barcode costs statistical power; a cell with the WRONG barcode moves a real phenotype onto another guide's average and is not recoverable downstream, because nothing later can tell it happened.

records.context: A pooled Toxoplasma CRISPR screening experiment has three noisy layers stacked on top of each other — which genotypes landed in which well, how many of a well's cells the microscope saw and how well the machine-learning classification model called them, and how many reads each genotype got out of the amplicon pool. The question a screener has to answer *before* spending the microscope time is "with this library, this many microplate sample positions, this many cells per well and a machine-learning classification model at 0.80/0.12, would I actually find a hit?". That is a statistical detection sensitivity analysis, and it is only answerable by simulation because no layer is analytically tractable once the other two are stacked on it.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate#3
records.source: A pooled Toxoplasma CRISPR screen has three noisy layers stacked on top of each other — which genotypes landed in which well, how many of a well's cells the microscope saw and how well the classifier called them, and how many reads each genotype got out of the amplicon pool. The question a screener has to answer *before* spending the microscope time is "with this library, this many wells, this many cells per well and a classifier at 0.80/0.12, would I actually find a hit?". That is a power analysis, and it is only answerable by simulation because no layer is analytically tractable once the other two are stacked on it.
records.translation: Un experimento de cribado de Toxoplasma CRISPR agrupado tiene tres capas ruidosas apiladas una encima de la otra — cuyos genotipos acabaron en qué pozo, cuántas células de un pozo vieron el microscopio y qué tan bien las llamó el modelo de clasificación de aprendizaje automático, y cuántas leen cada genograma que salió del grupo de amplicones. La pregunta que un cribador tiene que responder *antes* pasando el tiempo en el microscopio es "con esta biblioteca, estas muchas posiciones de muestra de microplacas, estas tantas células por pozo y un modelo de calificación de aprendizaje mecánico en 0,80/0,12, encontraría realmente un éxito?". Eso es un análisis de sensibilidad de detección estadística, y sólo es responsible por simulación porque ninguna capa es tratable analíticamente una vez que los otros dos se apilan en él.

records.context: **Well dropout from too few imaged cells** (:func:`drop_low_cell_wells`, ``min_cells_per_well=``). A well where the microscope found three cells enters the fit as one observation next to a well with four hundred. Its positive fraction can only be 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1, and its standard error is several times the machine-learning classification model's whole signal gap. The Poisson offset stops it dominating the scale of the fit; it does not stop its read-fraction covariate being paired with noise. Dropping such microplate sample positions is what an analyst does by hand, and it costs microplate sample positions — so which way the trade comes out is a thing to simulate rather than assert.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate#20
records.source: **Well dropout from too few imaged cells** (:func:`drop_low_cell_wells`, ``min_cells_per_well=``). A well where the microscope found three cells enters the fit as one observation next to a well with four hundred. Its positive fraction can only be 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1, and its standard error is several times the classifier's whole signal gap. The Poisson offset stops it dominating the scale of the fit; it does not stop its read-fraction covariate being paired with noise. Dropping such wells is what an analyst does by hand, and it costs wells — so which way the trade comes out is a thing to simulate rather than assert.
records.translation: **El abandono de muy pocas células de imágenes** (:func:`drop_low_cell_wells`, ``min_cells_per_well=``). Un pozo donde el microscopio encontró tres células entra en el ajuste como una observación junto a un pozo con cuatrocientas. Su fracción positiva sólo puede ser 0, 1/3, 2/3 o 1, y su error estándar es varias veces la brecha de señal del modelo de clasificación de aprendizaje automático. El desplazamiento de Poisson lo detiene dominando la escala del ajuste; no detiene su covariable lectura-fracción siendo emparejado con el ruido. La eliminación de tales posiciones de muestra de microplaca es lo que un analista hace a mano, y cuesta posiciones de la muestra de Microplaca — por lo que la manera en que el comercio sale es una cosa para simular en lugar de afirmar.

records.context: That product is used as a Bernoulli probability. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` for ``prob > 1`` with a warning, and the ``NA`` propagates into every downstream count. Clipping keeps the run alive, but it means the realised genes-per-microplate sample position is *below* the requested ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` for the affected genes, so the warning carries the clip count and the worst offender.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.AbundanceClippedWarning#1
records.source: That product is used as a Bernoulli probability. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` for ``prob > 1`` with a warning, and the ``NA`` propagates into every downstream count. Clipping keeps the run alive, but it means the realised genes-per-well is *below* the requested ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` for the affected genes, so the warning carries the clip count and the worst offender.
records.translation: Ese producto se utiliza como probabilidad Bernoulli. R ``rbinom`` devuelve ``NA`` para ``prob > 1`` con una advertencia, y el ``NA`` se propaga en cada conteo aguas abajo. El recorte mantiene la ejecución con vida, pero significa que la posición de la muestra de genes por microplaca realizada es *below* el ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` solicitado para los genes afectados, por lo que la advertencia lleva el recuento de clip y el peor delincuente.

records.source: Cross-*well* hopping — a read landing in the wrong sample entirely — is not modelled. It needs a plate-level index layout the simulator does not carry, and within-well gene confusion is the mechanism that dilutes the effect being measured.
records.translation: El salto entre *pocillos* — un aterrizaje de lectura en la muestra equivocada por completo — no se modela. Necesita un laboratorio microplaca-nivel de índice de diseño que el simulador no lleva, y la confusión génica dentro del pocillo es el mecanismo que diluye el efecto que se mide.

records.context: 1. Cells contributing DNA: ``gene_in_well * Count(lambda, var)``. This is normally far larger than the *imaged* count, because sequencing sees the whole well and the microscope sees a few microscope fields of view. 2. Amplification: one lognormal PCR factor per well, ``pcr_factor ~ LogNormal(meanlog=pcr_factor_mu, sdlog=sqrt(pcr_factor_var))``. Note both parameters are on the **log** scale despite their names; a ``pcr_factor_mu`` of 2.0 is a median amplification of ``exp(2) ~ 7.4``. The factor is per well, not per gene, because a well is one PCR reaction — which is exactly why read counts within a well are not independent. 3. Sequencing: reads are drawn from the amplified barcode pool **without replacement** (multivariate hypergeometric), because a finite flow cell reading a finite library is sampling without replacement, and modelling it as multinomial overstates how much independent information deep microplate sample positions carry. 4. **Mis-assignment**, when ``sequencing_error_rate > 0``: a fraction of the reads is credited to the wrong gene. Off by default, because it is not in the R and a silently different baseline would make every number already quoted from this module wrong. See :func:`misassign_reads` for what it models and why it always costs power.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_sequencing_plate#2
records.source: 1. Cells contributing DNA: ``gene_in_well * Count(lambda, var)``. This is normally far larger than the *imaged* count, because sequencing sees the whole well and the microscope sees a few fields. 2. Amplification: one lognormal PCR factor per well, ``pcr_factor ~ LogNormal(meanlog=pcr_factor_mu, sdlog=sqrt(pcr_factor_var))``. Note both parameters are on the **log** scale despite their names; a ``pcr_factor_mu`` of 2.0 is a median amplification of ``exp(2) ~ 7.4``. The factor is per well, not per gene, because a well is one PCR reaction — which is exactly why read counts within a well are not independent. 3. Sequencing: reads are drawn from the amplified barcode pool **without replacement** (multivariate hypergeometric), because a finite flow cell reading a finite library is sampling without replacement, and modelling it as multinomial overstates how much independent information deep wells carry. 4. **Mis-assignment**, when ``sequencing_error_rate > 0``: a fraction of the reads is credited to the wrong gene. Off by default, because it is not in the R and a silently different baseline would make every number already quoted from this module wrong. See :func:`misassign_reads` for what it models and why it always costs power.
records.translation: 1. Células que aportan DNA: ``gene_in_well * Count(lambda, var)``. Esto es normalmente mucho más grande que el conteo de *imaged*, porque la secuenciación ve todo el pozo y el microscopio ve algunos campos de visión del microscopio. 2. Amplificación: un factor PCR lognormal por pozo, ``pcr_factor ~ LogNormal(meanlog=pcr_factor_mu, sdlog=sqrt(pcr_factor_var))``. Note que ambos parámetros están en la escala **log** a pesar de sus nombres; un ``pcr_factor_mu`` de 2.0 es una amplificación mediana de ``exp(2) ~ 7.4``. El factor es por pozo no por gen, porque un pozo es una reacción PCR — que es exactamente por qué los recuentos de lectura dentro de un pozo no son independientes. 3. Secuenciación: las lecturas se extraen del pool de códigos de barras amplificados **sin reemplazo** (hipergeometría multivariable), porque una célula de flujo finito que lee una biblioteca finita es muestreo sin reemplazo, y modelarla como multinomio sobrestima la cantidad de información independiente que llevan las posiciones de muestra de microplacas profundas. 4. **Mis-asignación**, cuando ``sequencing_error_rate > 0``: una fracción de las lecturas es acreditada al gen incorrecto. De forma predeterminada, porque no está en la R y una línea de base silenciosamente diferente haría que cada número ya citado de este módulo se equivoca. Vea :func:`misassign_reads` por lo que modela y por qué siempre cuesta potencia.

records.context: **Two departures from the R original, both deliberate.** Upstream computes ``n_reads_per_well = round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` inside a ``group_by(well)``, so ``nrow`` is the *library size*: with 452 genes and ``n_reads_total = 128318`` that is 284 reads per well, against a real screening experiment near 3e4. The parameter is documented as "total reads in the screening experiment" in one vignette and "geometric mean of well reads" in another. This function takes ``n_reads_per_well`` unambiguously and reports ``n_reads_total`` as the derived sum. Second, upstream's guard ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)`` is computed from ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)`` while the urn is ``round(cells * pcr)`` element-wise; the two differ by rounding and the draw can ask for more balls than the urn holds. The guard here is computed from the urn itself.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_sequencing_plate#3
records.source: **Two departures from the R original, both deliberate.** Upstream computes ``n_reads_per_well = round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` inside a ``group_by(well)``, so ``nrow`` is the *library size*: with 452 genes and ``n_reads_total = 128318`` that is 284 reads per well, against a real screen near 3e4. The parameter is documented as "total reads in the screen" in one vignette and "geometric mean of well reads" in another. This function takes ``n_reads_per_well`` unambiguously and reports ``n_reads_total`` as the derived sum. Second, upstream's guard ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)`` is computed from ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)`` while the urn is ``round(cells * pcr)`` element-wise; the two differ by rounding and the draw can ask for more balls than the urn holds. The guard here is computed from the urn itself.
records.translation: **Dos salidas del original R, ambos deliberados.** Upstream calcula ``n_reads_per_well = round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` dentro de un ``group_by(well)``, por lo que ``nrow`` es el tamaño *biblioteca*: con 452 genes y ``n_reads_total = 128318`` que es 284 lecturas por pozo, en contra de un experimento de proyección real cerca de 3e4. El parámetro se documenta como "total lee en el experimento de cribado" en una viñeta y "media geométrica de las lecturas del pozo" en otra. Esta función toma ``n_reads_per_well`` sin ambigüedades e informa ``n_reads_total`` como la suma derivada. En segundo lugar, la protección de aguas arriba ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)`` se calcula a partir de ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)`` mientras que la urna es ``round(cells * pcr)`` elemento en sentido; los dos se diferencian redondeando y el dibujo puede pedir más bolas de las que la urna sostiene. El guardia aquí se calcula desde la urina misma.

records.context: Spectral unmixing comes first. With ``unmix`` on, a bleed-through matrix is estimated from the single-stain control microplate sample positions ``unmix_controls`` names and every raw microscope field of view is unmixed across all its image data channels before illumination correction, the PSF and the chain; the matrix joins the same record. Measure estimates its own over the measured image data channels and unmixes each microscope field of view before its preprocessing hooks, recording the matrix in the saved processing-session settings and ``measurements/bleed_through.json``.
records.label: spacr.psf_pipeline#3
records.source: Spectral unmixing comes first. With ``unmix`` on, a bleed-through matrix is estimated from the single-stain control wells ``unmix_controls`` names and every raw field is unmixed across all its channels before illumination correction, the PSF and the chain; the matrix joins the same record. Measure estimates its own over the measured channels and unmixes each field before its preprocessing hooks, recording the matrix in the saved run settings and ``measurements/bleed_through.json``.
records.translation: El desmezclado espectral es lo primero. Con ``unmix`` encendido, se estima una matriz de sangrado a través de las posiciones de muestra de microplacas de control de tinción única que nombra ``unmix_controls`` y cada campo de visión del microscopio en bruto no se mezcla en todos sus canales de datos de imagen antes de la corrección de iluminación, el PSF y la cadena; la matriz une el mismo registro. La medición estima su propio campo de vista sobre los canales de información de imagen medidos y desmixa cada campo visual del microscopio antes de sus ganchos de preprocesamiento, registrando la matriz en los ajustes guardados de la sesión de procesamiento y ``measurements/bleed_through.json``.

records.context: A bounded five-second join used to let the screen disappear while the daemon independent execution path still owned a live SQLite connection.  That is unsafe at application shutdown: CPython can finalize the sqlite extension while the independent execution path is still inside it.  SQLite already bounds lock waits with its 30-second connection timeout, so a requested blocking stop waits for the independent execution path to close its cursor and connection completely.
records.label: spacr.qt.annotate_engine.SaveWorker.stop#1
records.source: A bounded five-second join used to let the screen disappear while the daemon thread still owned a live SQLite connection.  That is unsafe at application shutdown: CPython can finalize the sqlite extension while the thread is still inside it.  SQLite already bounds lock waits with its 30-second connection timeout, so a requested blocking stop waits for the thread to close its cursor and connection completely.
records.translation: Una unión de cinco segundos limitada utilizada para dejar que la pantalla desaparezca mientras que la ruta de ejecución independiente del demonio todavía poseía una conexión SQLite en vivo. Eso es inseguro en el apagado de la aplicación: CPython puede finalizar la extensión sqlite mientras la ruta independiente de ejecución está todavía dentro de ella. SQLite ya limita el bloqueo espera con su tiempo de conexión de 30 segundos, por lo que una parada de bloqueo solicitada espera a que la trayectoria de ejecución autónoma cierre completamente su cursor y conexión.

records.translation: Un módulo plegado en un host mantiene su nombre de datos estructurados en todas partes donde se guarda un nombre de dato estructurado: un diario de sesión de procesamiento, el registro de reinicio de fuerza, ``spacr-qt <app>`` en el historial de shell de alguien. Ese nombre de información estructurada ya no nombra una vista de aplicación, y navegar directamente hacia ella construiría una -- una página huérfana sin fila de barra lateral, sin mosaico y sin vuelta a ella.

records.translation: Tres cosas no siguen una llamada ``setStyleSheet``: los mosaicos Home establecen tamaños/margenes de la escala de fuentes en Python, cada QIcon hornea su pixmap en el tema en vigor cuando se construyó, y el modo del muelle y la opacidad de la página son decisiones de diseño en lugar de colores. records.context: Extracted image region PNGs are not ordinary images. Anything spaCR wrote before the BGR fix has the first stain in the *blue* image data channel, and a 16-bit single-image data channel extracted image region opened with ``convert('RGB')`` is clipped to solid white by PIL. Both are corrected by :func:`spacr.qt.annotate_engine.load_crop_image`, which is therefore the only loader used here, so a hover preview shows the same colours as the annotation grid.
records.label: spacr.qt.crop_thumbs#7
records.source: Crop PNGs are not ordinary images. Anything spaCR wrote before the BGR fix has the first stain in the *blue* channel, and a 16-bit single-channel crop opened with ``convert('RGB')`` is clipped to solid white by PIL. Both are corrected by :func:`spacr.qt.annotate_engine.load_crop_image`, which is therefore the only loader used here, so a hover preview shows the same colours as the annotation grid.
records.translation: Región de imagen extraída PNGs no son imágenes ordinarias. Cualquier cosa que spaCR escribiera antes de la corrección BGR tiene la primera tinción en el canal de datos de imagen *blue*, y una región de imagen extraída de un canal de 16 bits abierta con ``convert('RGB')`` se corta en blanco sólido por PIL. Ambos se corrigen por :func:`spacr.qt.annotate_engine.load_crop_image`, que es por lo tanto el único cargador utilizado aquí, por lo que una vista previa hover muestra los mismos colores que la cuadrícula de anotación.

records.context: The interpreter collects generation *n* when that generation's count passes its threshold, youngest first, and collecting a generation also clears the younger ones. Reproducing that here -- rather than calling a full ``gc.collect()`` on every tick -- is what keeps the cost the same as it was before this module existed. A full sweep every second would walk every live numpy array in the process.
records.label: spacr.qt.gc_policy.collect_once#1
records.source: The interpreter collects generation *n* when that generation's count passes its threshold, youngest first, and collecting a generation also clears the younger ones. Reproducing that here -- rather than calling a full ``gc.collect()`` on every tick -- is what keeps the cost the same as it was before this module existed. A full sweep every second would walk every live numpy array in the process.
records.translation: El intérprete recoge la generación *n* cuando el conteo de esa generación supera su umbral, el más joven primero, y la recolección de una generación también elimina a los más jóvenes. La reproducción de que aquí -- en lugar de llamar a un completo ``gc.collect()`` en cada ciclo -- es lo que mantiene el costo igual que antes de que existiera este módulo. Un barrido completo cada segundo caminaría cada matriz numpy en vivo en el proceso.

records.context: What is not live, and why that was accepted. Every size the font scale pins from Python -- row heights, column widths, icon sizes, tile geometry, all of :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.scaled_px` -- moves only when the stylesheet is rebuilt, and that is the 587 ms number. The choice made: "Text live, spacing on release." Text follows the wheel; the spacing around it catches up in one step when the wheel stops or Z comes up. It is a deliberate compromise, not an oversight, and it is why the settle exists.
records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom#7
records.source: WHAT IS NOT LIVE, AND WHY THAT WAS ACCEPTED. Every size the font scale pins from Python -- row heights, column widths, icon sizes, tile geometry, all of :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.scaled_px` -- moves only when the stylesheet is rebuilt, and that is the 587 ms number. The choice made: "Text live, spacing on release." Text follows the wheel; the spacing around it catches up in one step when the wheel stops or Z comes up. It is a deliberate compromise, not an oversight, and it is why the settle exists.
records.translation: Lo que no está en vivo, y por qué se aceptó. Cada tamaño de los pines de escala de fuentes de Python -- alturas de fila, anchos de columna, tamaños de iconos, geometría de mosaicos, todo :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.scaled_px` -- se mueve sólo cuando se reconstruye la hoja de estilos, y ese es el número de 587 ms. La elección hecha: "Texto en directo, espaciado en el lanzamiento". El texto sigue la rueda; el espaciamiento alrededor de ella se alcanza en un solo paso cuando la rueda se detiene o se levanta Z. Es un compromiso deliberado, no una supervisión, y es por eso que existe el arreglo.

records.context: Installed on the QApplication because the gesture has to work on every screen -- a per-screen handler works in some places and not others, which is the complaint that produced 315's warning about application filters. That warning is about COST, so the body is two integer comparisons for an event it does not want, and the wheel branch is not even reached unless Z is down. Measured at 1.2 us per uninteresting event on this machine, which is the Python call itself rather than anything this does inside it. Create the filter that scales the interface while the key is held.
records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom.LiveZoomFilter#1
records.source: Installed on the QApplication because the gesture has to work on every screen -- a per-screen handler works in some places and not others, which is the complaint that produced 315's warning about application filters. Measured at 1.2 us per uninteresting event on this machine, which is the Python call itself rather than anything this does inside it. Create the filter that scales the interface while the key is held.
records.translation: Instalado en la QApplication porque el gesto tiene que funcionar en cada pantalla -- un manejador por pantalla funciona en algunos lugares y no en otros, que es la queja que produjo la advertencia de 315 sobre filtros de aplicación. Esa advertencia es sobre COST, por lo que el cuerpo es dos comparaciones enteras para un evento que no quiere, y la rama de la rueda ni siquiera se alcanza a menos que Z esté abajo. Medido en 1,2 nosotros por evento poco interesante en esta máquina, que se llama a sí mismo Python en lugar de cualquier cosa que esto hace dentro de ella. Cree el filtro que escala la interfaz mientras se mantiene la clave.

records.context: This is the tool a brush is not. A brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a cell's rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background; ``draw`` closes the path (last point back to the first) and fills what it encloses, so one gesture produces one solid object with one id. Anything already labelled inside the outline is overwritten, which is the point: the outline asserts "all of this is one object".

records.source: This is the tool a brush is not. A brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a cell's rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background; ``draw`` closes the path (last point back to the first) and fills what it encloses, so one gesture produces one solid object with one id. Anything already labelled inside the outline is overwritten, which is the point: the outline asserts "all of this is one object".
records.translation: Esta es la herramienta que un pincel no es. Un cepillo estampillas discos a lo largo del camino, por lo que el trazado del borde de una célula con él etiqueta el borde y deja el fondo medio; ``draw`` cierra el camino (último punto de vuelta a la primera) y llena lo que encierra, así que un gesto produce un objeto sólido con un id. Cualquier cosa ya etiquetada dentro del contorno está sobreescrito, que es el punto: el esquema afirma "todo esto es un objeto".

records.context: What this reaches and what it does not. It is the colour of the figure's CHROME: the axis spines and the tick marks. The control that DOES reach the data's lines is the per-figure one (:func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_settings.apply_line_colour`), which is a user asking for it about one figure -- the same division as the pyqtgraph side, where the theme sets `_foreground` and `set_line_colour` is a menu entry.

The control that DOES reach the data's lines is the per-figure one (:func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_settings.apply_line_colour`), which is a user asking for it about one figure -- the same division as the pyqtgraph side, where the theme sets `_foreground` and `set_line_colour` is a menu entry.
records.translation: Lo que esto alcanza y lo que no. Es el color de la CROME de la figura: las espinas del eje y las marcas. records.context: The banner **reads** a verdict; it does not compute one.  Opening a plate's masks takes seconds to minutes, which is too slow for every visit to the screen.  So :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` parses the CSVs the mask run already wrote, dates each one against its mask stack, and reports a card older than its masks as out of date instead of using it.  Only the *Score the masks now* button scores anything, only when pressed, and it does it on a background execution unit and writes the card so the next open is cheap again.

records.source: The banner **reads** a verdict; it does not compute one.  Opening a plate's masks takes seconds to minutes, which is too slow for every visit to the screen.  So :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` parses the CSVs the mask run already wrote, dates each one against its mask stack, and reports a card older than its masks as out of date instead of using it.  Only the *Score the masks now* button scores anything, only when pressed, and it does it on a worker thread and writes the card so the next open is cheap again.
records.translation: El banner **reads** un veredicto; no calcula uno. Abrir las máscaras de una placa toma segundos a minutos, que es demasiado lento para cada visita a la pantalla. Así que :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` analiza el CSVs la ejecución de la máscara ya escribió, fecha cada uno contra su pila de máscaras, e informa de una tarjeta más antigua que sus máscaras como desactualizada en lugar de usarlo. Sólo el *Score las mascaras ahora* botón puntúa cualquier cosa, sólo cuando se presiona, y lo hace en una unidad de ejecución de fondo y escribe la tarjeta para que el siguiente abierto de nuevo es barato.

All of it is I/O on a path the user supplied.
