records.source: ``(centre, scale, note)``. ``note`` is ``""`` when the MAD did the work, ``"mad-zero"`` when the fallback fired, ``"constant"`` when the feature has no variation at all (scale 0, nothing can be an outlier), and ``"empty"`` when there is nothing finite to measure.
records.translation: ``(centre, scale, note)``. ``note`` es ``""`` cuando el MAD hizo el trabajo, ``"mad-zero"`` cuando se disparó la copia de seguridad, ``"constant"`` cuando la característica no tiene variación alguna (escala 0, nada puede ser un valor atípico), y ``"empty"`` cuando no hay nada finito que medir.

records.context: Every feature loading with the same sign is the classic "size" factor of morphometrics: one end big objects, the other end small ones. It is real, it is usually PC1, and it is usually a statement about segmentation and focus rather than about biology — so it is detected and said out loud rather than left for the reader to notice.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.is_size_like#1
records.source: Every feature loading with the same sign is the classic "size" factor of morphometrics: one end big objects, the other end small ones. It is real, it is usually PC1, and it is usually a statement about segmentation and focus rather than about biology — so it is detected and said out loud rather than left for the reader to notice.
records.translation: Cada característica que carga con el mismo signo es el factor clásico "size" de la morfometría: un extremo objetos grandes, el otro extremo pequeños. Es real, generalmente es PC1, y suele ser una declaración sobre la segmentación y el enfoque en lugar de sobre la biología — por lo que se detecta y se dice en voz alta en lugar de dejar que el lector se dé cuenta.

records.context: Ranked by ``r_x² + r_y²`` — how much of the feature is visible in this image layer at all. Drawing the other four hundred arrows would say nothing except that the figure is full; drawing the *longest* ones is the standard choice because a short arrow means "this feature points somewhere you are not looking", not "this feature does not matter".
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.plane_features#1
records.source: Ranked by ``r_x² + r_y²`` — how much of the feature is visible in this plane at all. Drawing the other four hundred arrows would say nothing except that the figure is full; drawing the *longest* ones is the standard choice because a short arrow means "this feature points somewhere you are not looking", not "this feature does not matter".
records.translation: Clasificado por ``r_x² + r_y²`` — cuánto de la característica es visible en esta capa de imagen en absoluto. Dibujar las otras cuatrocientas flechas no diría nada excepto que la figura está llena; dibujar las *longest* es la opción estándar porque una flecha corta significa "esta característica apunta a algún lugar que no estás buscando", no "esta característica no importa".

records.context: Everything that took work in the Graph Builder therefore already works here and cannot drift out of step with it: the shared-scale facet grid, the fixed categorical colour order, the large-data policy and its notice, the selection-dims-never-hides rule, and the brush. Because the scores frame carries the object identifier columns, a rectangle dragged around a cluster in PC space publishes a real :class:`~spacr.selection.Selection`, and the UMAP, the laboratory microplate map and the extracted-image-region grid highlight the same cells. Reimplementing a scatter here would have meant reimplementing all of that and getting the brush subtly wrong.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_view#4
records.source: Everything that took work in the Graph Builder therefore already works here and cannot drift out of step with it: the shared-scale facet grid, the fixed categorical colour order, the large-data policy and its notice, the selection-dims-never-hides rule, and the brush. Because the scores frame carries the object key columns, a rectangle dragged around a cluster in PC space publishes a real :class:`~spacr.selection.Selection`, and the UMAP, the plate map and the crop grid highlight the same cells. Reimplementing a scatter here would have meant reimplementing all of that and getting the brush subtly wrong.
records.translation: Por lo tanto, todo lo que funcionó en el Graph Builder ya funciona aquí y no puede salirse del paso con él: la cuadrícula de facetas de escala compartida, el orden de color categórico fijo, la política de grandes datos y su aviso, la regla de selección-dimite-nunca-oculta, y el pincel. Debido a que el marco de puntuaciones lleva las columnas de identificador de objetos, un rectángulo arrastrado alrededor de un cluster en el espacio PC publica un :class:`~spacr.selection.Selection` real, y el UMAP, el mapa de microplacas de laboratorio y la cuadrícula de la región de imagen extraída resaltan las mismas células. La aplicación de una dispersión aquí habría significado la aplicación de todo eso y conseguir el cepillo sutilmente mal.

records.context: :mod:`spacr.power_simulate` and :mod:`spacr.power_model` answer the question *"given these sixteen parameters, how well does the model recover the hits?"*. records.context: Filtering changes a Q-Q plot in a way it does not change a volcano. A volcano of the guides is the same dots with some removed; a Q-Q of the guides is a different diagnostic -- the expected quantiles are recomputed over 900 tests instead of 1,200, so the diagonal moves, the inflation figure at the median is a different number, and the excess in the histogram's first bin is this family's excess and not the run's. A reader who does not know which one is on application view cannot use either.

records.source: Filtering changes a Q-Q plot in a way it does not change a volcano. A volcano of the guides is the same dots with some removed; a Q-Q of the guides is a different diagnostic -- the expected quantiles are recomputed over 900 tests instead of 1,200, so the diagonal moves, the inflation figure at the median is a different number, and the excess in the histogram's first bin is this family's excess and not the run's. A reader who does not know which one is on screen cannot use either.
records.translation: Filtrar cambia una trama Q-Q de una manera que no cambia un volcán. Un volcán de los guías es los mismos puntos con algunos removidos; Un Q-Q de las guías es un diagnóstico diferente -- los cuantiles esperados se recomponen en 900 pruebas en lugar de 1.200, por lo que los movimientos diagonales, la cifra de inflación en la mediana es un número diferente, y el exceso en el primer cubo del histograma es el exceso de esta familia y no el de la ejecución. Un lector que no sabe cuál está en la vista de la aplicación tampoco puede utilizarla.

A segmentation preview has four things worth looking at: the image with the outlines on it, the label masks alone, the flow microscope field of view the masks were pooled from, and the cell probability the flow was thresholded at. Mask generation's live preview showed three of them through a dropdown; the plaque preview showed its own four through tabs, drawn by its own code. This module is the one place both can draw them from, so that a change to how a cell probability is coloured reaches both previews at once.

records.source: One widget serves two owners. A segmentation preview has four things worth looking at: the image with the outlines on it, the label masks alone, the flow field the masks were pooled from, and the cell probability the flow was thresholded at. Mask generation's live preview showed three of them through a dropdown; the plaque preview showed its own four through tabs, drawn by its own code. This module is the one place both can draw them from, so that a change to how a cell probability is coloured reaches both previews at once.
records.translation: Un widget sirve a dos propietarios. Una vista previa de la segmentación tiene cuatro cosas que vale la pena mirar: la imagen con los contornos en ella, las máscaras de la etiqueta solo, el campo de flujo a partir del cual se agruparon las máscaras, y la probabilidad de la célula el flujo fue umbral en. Previsualización en vivo de la generación de máscaras mostró tres de ellos a través de un desplegable; la vista previa placa mostró sus propias cuatro a través pestañas, dibujado por su propio código. Este módulo es el único lugar ambos pueden dibujarlos, de modo que un cambio a cómo una probabilidad de célula se colorea alcanza ambos previsualizaciones a la vez.

records.context: **Per-frame masks are cached** under a *segmentation signature* — the source path, the frame indices, and every setting that can change a label image (model, image data channel, diameter, flow threshold, cell probability, normalisation). Change a *tracking* setting and the signature is unchanged, the cache hits, and only :func:`link_tracks` runs. Change a segmentation setting and the signature moves, so the masks are rebuilt.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#2
records.source: **Per-frame masks are cached** under a *segmentation signature* — the source path, the frame indices, and every setting that can change a label image (model, channel, diameter, flow threshold, cell probability, normalisation). Change a *tracking* setting and the signature is unchanged, the cache hits, and only :func:`link_tracks` runs. Change a segmentation setting and the signature moves, so the masks are rebuilt.
records.translation: Las máscaras de **Per-frame son caché** bajo una firma de *segmentation* — la ruta de origen, los índices de marco y cada configuración que puede cambiar una imagen de etiqueta (modelo, canal de datos de imagen, diámetro, umbral de flujo, probabilidad de célula, normalización). Cambie un ajuste de *tracking* y la firma no cambia, la caché golpea y sólo se ejecuta :func:`link_tracks`. Cambie una configuración de segmentación y se mueve la firma, por lo que las máscaras se reconstruyen.

records.context: **Shared axes by default.** Two panels whose y axes differ by an order of magnitude look identical, so a per-panel autoscale turns "the knockdown halved the count" into "the two panels look the same". Every scale here is computed over the whole grid unless the user explicitly asks otherwise, and when they do ask otherwise :attr:`Trellis.notice` says so in words, so a free-scale trellis copied into a slide still states that its scales differ. :data:`SCALE_ROW` and :data:`SCALE_COL` are the middle grounds: panels down a column of the grid share, or panels across a row do, which is what you want when the rows are three different measurements and the columns are three conditions.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec#2
records.source: **Shared axes by default.** Two panels whose y axes differ by an order of magnitude look identical, so a per-panel autoscale turns "the knockdown halved the count" into "the two panels look the same". Every scale here is computed over the whole grid unless the user explicitly asks otherwise, and when they do ask otherwise :attr:`Trellis.notice` says so in words, so a free-scale trellis copied into a slide still states that its scales differ. :data:`SCALE_ROW` and :data:`SCALE_COL` are the middle grounds: panels down a column of the grid share, or panels across a row do, which is what you want when the rows are three different measurements and the columns are three conditions.
records.translation: **Ejes compartidos por defecto.** Dos paneles cuyos ejes y difieren por un orden de magnitud se ven idénticos, por lo que una escala automática por panel convierte "la reducción a la mitad del conteo" en "los dos paneles se ven iguales".Cada escala aquí se calcula sobre toda la cuadrícula a menos que el usuario pregunte explícitamente lo contrario, y cuando preguntan lo contrario :attr:`Trellis.notice` lo dice en palabras, así que un enrejado a escala libre copiado en una diapositiva todavía afirma que sus escalas difieren. :data:`SCALE_ROW` y :data:`SCALE_COL` son los terrenos centrales: paneles abajo de una columna de la cuadricula compartida, o paneles a través de una fila hacer, que es lo que quieres cuando las filas son tres mediciones diferentes y las columnas son tres condiciones.

records.context: "Already measured" deliberately means *present in every table this processing session writes*, not "present somewhere". ``_measure_crop_core`` inserts into ``cell``, then ``nucleus``, then ``pathogen``, then ``cytoplasm``, then ``png_list``, one call after another with a commit each — so a process killed between two of those calls leaves a field that has cell rows and no nucleus rows. Counting that field as done would permanently lose its nuclei; counting it as pending without clearing it first would duplicate its cells. It is reported through ``partial`` so the caller can do the third, correct thing: clear it and execute it again.
records.label: spacr.resume.completed_fields_in_db#1
records.source: "Already measured" deliberately means *present in every table this run writes*, not "present somewhere". ``_measure_crop_core`` inserts into ``cell``, then ``nucleus``, then ``pathogen``, then ``cytoplasm``, then ``png_list``, one call after another with a commit each — so a process killed between two of those calls leaves a field that has cell rows and no nucleus rows. Counting that field as done would permanently lose its nuclei; counting it as pending without clearing it first would duplicate its cells. It is reported through ``partial`` so the caller can do the third, correct thing: clear it and re-run it.
records.translation: "Already measured" deliberadamente significa *presente en cada tabla esta sesión de procesamiento escribe*, no "present somewhere". ``_measure_crop_core`` inserta en ``cell``, luego ``nucleus``, luego ``pathogen``, luego ``cytoplasm``, luego ``png_list``, una llamada tras otra con un commit cada uno — por lo que un proceso matado entre dos de esas llamadas deja un campo que tiene filas de células y no filas de núcleo. Contando ese campo como hecho perdería permanentemente sus núcleos; contándolo como pendiente sin limpiar primero duplicaría sus células. Se informa a través de ``partial`` para que el llamante pueda hacer la tercera, cosa correcta: limpiarlo y ejecutarlo de nuevo.

records.context: Every number here rests on one choice: when is a predicted object the same object as a labelled one? The literature's answer is an IoU threshold, and the threshold is not a detail -- a model that finds every cell and outlines them loosely scores well at 0.5 and badly at 0.9, and a model that finds half of them perfectly does the opposite. That is why :func:`average_precision` reports the whole sweep from 0.5 to 0.9 rather than one number, and why every precision/recall figure states the threshold it was matched at.
records.label: spacr.scorecard#6
records.source: Every number here rests on one choice: when is a predicted object THE SAME object as a labelled one? The literature's answer is an IoU threshold, and the threshold is not a detail -- a model that finds every cell and outlines them loosely scores well at 0.5 and badly at 0.9, and a model that finds half of them perfectly does the opposite. That is why :func:`average_precision` reports the whole sweep from 0.5 to 0.9 rather than one number, and why every precision/recall figure states the threshold it was matched at.
records.translation: Cada número aquí se basa en una opción: ¿cuándo es un objeto predicho el mismo objeto que un objeto etiquetado? La respuesta de la literatura es un umbral IoU, y el umbral no es un detalle -- un modelo que encuentra cada célula y los esboza vagamente puntúa bien en 0.5 y mal en 0.9, y un modelo donde se encuentra la mitad de ellos perfectamente hace lo contrario. Es por eso que :func:`average_precision` reporta todo el barrido de 0.5 a 0.9 en lugar de un número, y por qué cada figura de precisión/recuerdo indica el umbral en el que fue emparejado.

records.context: A predicted boundary pixel counts as correct when a true boundary pixel lies within ``tolerance`` pixels of it, and vice versa. records.source: A predicted boundary pixel counts as correct when a true boundary pixel lies within ``tolerance`` pixels of it, and vice versa. records.translation: Un píxel límite predicho cuenta como correcto cuando un píxEL límite verdadero se encuentra dentro de ``tolerance`` píxeles de él, y viceversa. Una tolerancia se utiliza porque dos personas que etiquetan la misma célula no están de acuerdo con un pízel o dos, por lo que una puntuación límite de tolerancia cero mide el anotador tanto como el modelo.

records.context: The **Map Barcodes** module connects a sequencing run to an image-based application view.  It finds the laboratory microplate-column, guide, and laboratory microplate-row barcode in each read, resolves those sequences against reference tables, and counts the resulting guides by well.  :func:`generate_barecode_mapping` is the GUI and Python entry point (the historical ``barecode`` spelling remains part of the public API); :func:`graph_sequencing_stats` can then help choose a read-fraction cutoff.
records.label: spacr.sequencing#2
records.source: The **Map Barcodes** module connects a sequencing run to an image-based screen.  It finds the plate-column, guide, and plate-row barcode in each read, resolves those sequences against reference tables, and counts the resulting guides by well.  :func:`generate_barecode_mapping` is the GUI and Python entry point (the historical ``barecode`` spelling remains part of the public API); :func:`graph_sequencing_stats` can then help choose a read-fraction cutoff.
records.translation: El módulo **Map Barcodes** conecta una secuenciación a una vista de aplicación basada en imágenes. Encuentra la microplaca de laboratorio, guía y microplacas de laboratorio en cada lectura, resuelve esas secuencias contra tablas de referencia y cuenta las guías resultantes por pocillo. :func:`generate_barecode_mapping` es el punto de entrada GUI y Python (la ortografía histórica ``barecode`` sigue siendo parte del público API); :func:`graph_sequencing_stats` puede entonces ayudar a elegir un corte de fracción de lectura.

records.context: Plaque analysis accepts a folder of TIFF images, or existing masks beneath that folder, plus Cellpose settings and a bundled, catalogue, or local plaque model.  Recruitment starts from a spaCR ``measurements.db`` containing joined cell, nucleus, pathogen, and cytoplasm features; it needs a fluorescence image data channel, object filters, and laboratory microplate metadata that assign cell type, pathogen, and treatment.  Invasion and Replication both need one row per segmented parasite in a measurement table and condition metadata.  Invasion additionally needs the outside- and total-stain image data channels and preferably known control microplate sample positions; Replication needs a defensible ``vacuole_key`` or spatial-linking distance. The Cellpose utilities require paired images and masks for training/testing, or an image folder and model path for inference.
records.label: spacr.submodules#4
records.source: Plaque analysis accepts a folder of TIFF images, or existing masks beneath that folder, plus Cellpose settings and a bundled, catalogue, or local plaque model.  Recruitment starts from a spaCR ``measurements.db`` containing joined cell, nucleus, pathogen, and cytoplasm features; it needs a fluorescence channel, object filters, and plate metadata that assign cell type, pathogen, and treatment.  Invasion and Replication both need one row per segmented parasite in a measurement table and condition metadata.  Invasion additionally needs the outside- and total-stain channels and preferably known control wells; Replication needs a defensible ``vacuole_key`` or spatial-linking distance. The Cellpose utilities require paired images and masks for training/testing, or an image folder and model path for inference.
records.translation: El análisis de placa acepta una carpeta de imágenes TIFF, o máscaras existentes debajo de esa carpeta, además de los ajustes Cellpose y un modelo de placa empaquetado, catálogo o local. El reclutamiento comienza desde un spaCR ``measurements.db`` que contiene características de célula, núcleo, patógeno y citoplasma unidos; necesita un canal de datos de imagen de fluorescencia, filtros de objeto y metadatos de microplaca de laboratorio que asignen tipo de célula, patógeno, y tratamiento. La invasión y replicación ambas necesitan una fila por parásito segmentado en una tabla de medición y metadatos sobre condiciones. Además, la invasión necesita los canales de datos de imagen de tinción exterior y total y posiciones de muestra de micro placas de control preferiblemente conocidas; La replicación necesita una distancia defensible ``vacuole_key`` o distancia de enlace espacial. Las utilidades Cellpose requieren imágenes emparejadas y máscaras para entrenamiento/prueba, o una carpeta de imagen y ruta de modelo para inferencia.

records.context: Plaque analysis writes ``<src>/masks/plaques_analysis.db`` with ``summary``, ``stats``, and ``details`` tables.  Recruitment returns per-object and per-well DataFrames and writes their CSVs and plots.  Invasion returns per-parasite classifications, per-microscope field of view thresholds and QC, per-well efficiencies, condition summaries and comparisons, controls, and figures; saved runs place those artifacts under ``results/analyze_invasion``. Replication returns per-vacuole counts, well and condition distributions, pairwise and omnibus statistics, figures, and the grouping method actually used, with saved output under ``results/analyze_replication``.  Model utilities produce trained weights, evaluation tables, masks, and object summaries as appropriate.
records.label: spacr.submodules#6
records.source: Plaque analysis writes ``<src>/masks/plaques_analysis.db`` with ``summary``, ``stats``, and ``details`` tables. Invasion returns per-parasite classifications, per-field thresholds and QC, per-well efficiencies, condition summaries and comparisons, controls, and figures; saved runs place those artifacts under ``results/analyze_invasion``. Replication returns per-vacuole counts, well and condition distributions, pairwise and omnibus statistics, figures, and the grouping method actually used, with saved output under ``results/analyze_replication``.  Model utilities produce trained weights, evaluation tables, masks, and object summaries as appropriate.
records.translation: El análisis de placa escribe ``<src>/masks/plaques_analysis.db`` con tablas ``summary``, ``stats`` y ``details``. Reclutamiento devuelve por objeto y por pozo DataFrames y escribe sus CSVs y parcelas. La invasión devuelve clasificaciones por parásito, umbrales de campo de visión por microscopio y QC, eficiencias por pozo, resúmenes de condiciones y comparaciones, controles y cifras; ejecuta guardados colocan esos artefactos bajo ``results/analyze_invasion``. Replicación devuelve recuentos por vacuola, distribuciones por pozo y condición, estadísticas de pares y ómnibus, cifras y el método de agrupamiento realmente utilizado, con salida guardada bajo ``results/analyze_replication``. Las utilidades modelo producen pesos entrenados, tablas de evaluación, máscaras y resúmenes de objetos según corresponda.

records.context: The analysis unit matters.  Invasion is inferred from *absence* of outside stain, so weak staining can only inflate the invaded fraction; thresholds are therefore recorded per field and statistics use microplate sample positions rather than treating parasites from one microplate sample position as independent replicates.  Replication groups by vacuole, not by host cell, because one cell can contain several vacuoles; 3, 5, 6, and 7 parasites remain in an explicit non-power-of-two QC bucket instead of being rounded into a biologically expected class.  Plaque area is calibrated against the microplate sample position scale when available, so comparisons should retain the acquisition metadata that defines that scale.
records.label: spacr.submodules#9
records.source: The analysis unit matters.  Invasion is inferred from *absence* of outside stain, so weak staining can only inflate the invaded fraction; thresholds are therefore recorded per field and statistics use wells rather than treating parasites from one well as independent replicates.  Replication groups by vacuole, not by host cell, because one cell can contain several vacuoles; 3, 5, 6, and 7 parasites remain in an explicit non-power-of-two QC bucket instead of being rounded into a biologically expected class.  Plaque area is calibrated against the well scale when available, so comparisons should retain the acquisition metadata that defines that scale.
records.translation: La unidad de análisis importa. La invasión se infiere de *ausencia* de la tinción exterior, por lo que la tinción débil sólo puede inflar la fracción invadida; por lo tanto, los umbrales se registran por campo y las estadísticas utilizan posiciones de muestra de microplacas en lugar de tratar los parásitos de una posición de muestra microplaca como réplicas independientes. Grupos de replicación por vacuola, no por célula huésped, porque una célula puede contener varias vacuolas; 3, 5, 6 y 7 parásitos permanecen en un cubo explícito sin poder de dos QC en vez de ser redondeados en una clase biológicamente esperada. El área de placa se calibra contra la escala de posición de la muestra micro plaquita cuando se dispone de ella, por ello las comparaciones deben retener los metadatos de adquisición que definen esa escala.

records.context: The rows come from :func:`spacr.io._read_and_merge_data`, which collapses the per-object ``pathogen`` table onto the **host cell** (``prcfo`` is built from ``cell_id``). ``pathogen_area`` on each row is therefore the *sum* of the areas of every pathogen object inside that host cell — one host cell carrying two parasitophorous vacuoles contributes a single row holding the combined area of both.

records.source: The rows come from :func:`spacr.io._read_and_merge_data`, which collapses the per-object ``pathogen`` table onto the **host cell** (``prcfo`` is built from ``cell_id``). ``pathogen_area`` on each row is therefore the *sum* of the areas of every pathogen object inside that host cell — one host cell carrying two parasitophorous vacuoles contributes a single row holding the combined area of both.
records.translation: Las filas vienen de :func:`spacr.io._read_and_merge_data`, que colapsa la tabla ``pathogen`` por objeto en la célula **huésped** (``prcfo`` se construye a partir de ``cell_id``). ``pathogen_area`` en cada fila es por lo tanto la *sum* de las áreas de cada objeto patógeno dentro de esa célula huésped — una célula huésped que lleva dos vacuolas parasitoforas contribuye a una sola fila que sostiene el área combinada de ambos.

Before permeabilisation an antibody reaches only the parasites still **outside** the host cell, so those are positive in both image data channels; the cells are then permeabilised and a second antibody stains **all** parasites, so a parasite positive only in the post-permeabilisation image data channel was inside. Hence:

records.source: The red/green invasion assay stains twice. Before permeabilisation an antibody reaches only the parasites still **outside** the host cell, so those are positive in both channels; the cells are then permeabilised and a second antibody stains **all** parasites, so a parasite positive only in the post-permeabilisation channel was inside. Hence:
records.translation: El ensayo de invasión rojo/verde tiñe dos veces. Antes de la permeabilización, un anticuerpo sólo alcanza los parásitos todavía **fuera** de la célula huésped, por lo que estos son positivos en ambos canales de datos de imagen; las células se permeabilizan entonces y un segundo anticuerpo tiñe **todos** los parásitos, de modo que un parásito positivo sólo en el canal de datos postpermeabilizatorio estaba dentro. Por lo tanto:

records.translation: **Los controles prevalecen sobre el método automático.** ``control_wells`` nombra posiciones de muestra microplaca cuyos parásitos no llevan tinción exterior; el umbral es entonces un cuantil alto de esa distribución negativa (``control_quantile``), las posiciones de la muestra micro placa de control se excluyen de los resultados, y ``threshold_source`` dice ``'control'`` por lo que el informe no puede confundirse con una ejecución automática.

records.context: Pooled screens provide guide counts for each microplate sample position, not a guide identity for each cell. This module combines those count constraints with similarity in measurement space. It selects high-confidence anchor cells, propagates their labels over a k-nearest-neighbour graph, and projects the result onto the per-microplate sample position guide fractions reported by sequencing.
records.label: spacr.sudoku#1
records.source: Pooled screens provide guide counts for each well, not a guide identity for each cell. This module combines those count constraints with similarity in measurement space. It selects high-confidence anchor cells, propagates their labels over a k-nearest-neighbour graph, and projects the result onto the per-well guide fractions reported by sequencing.
records.translation: Las cribados agrupadas proporcionan recuentos de guías para cada posición de muestra de microplaca, no una identidad de guía para cada célula. Este módulo combina esas limitaciones de recuento con la similitud en el espacio de medición. Selecciona células de anclaje de alta confianza, propaga sus etiquetas sobre un gráfico de k-nearest-neighbour, y proyecta el resultado en las fracciones de guía de posición de muestras por placa reportadas por secuenciación.

records.context: The propagation and class-mass normalization follow the label-propagation framework described by Zhu and Ghahramani (2003) and Zhou et al. (2004). The implementation has no trained graph-model weights; each result can be traced to its anchors and the sequencing constraint.
records.label: spacr.sudoku#4
records.source: The propagation and class-mass normalization follow the label-propagation framework described by Zhu and Ghahramani (2003) and Zhou et al. (2004). The implementation has no trained graph-model weights; each result can be traced to its anchors and the sequencing constraint.
records.translation: La normalización de la propagación y la masa de clase sigue el marco de propagación de etiquetas descrito por Zhu y Ghahramani (2003) y Zhou et al. (2004). La implementación no tiene pesos de modelos de grafos entrenados; cada resultado se puede rastrear a sus anclajes y la restricción de secuenciación.

records.context: Cellpose predicts, per pixel, a flow toward the centre of the object the pixel belongs to. Timeflows adds the same idea through time: per pixel of frame ``t``, where the centre of that object is in frame ``t+1``, and whether it has a successor at all (cells die, divide, leave the microscope field of view). Linking objects between frames then reads the model instead of guessing from overlap, which is where the plain IoU stitcher fails: fast cells that move more than their own size between frames (the MuSC movies move 3-4 diameters per frame at p95).
records.label: spacr.timeflows_model#1
records.source: Cellpose predicts, per pixel, a flow toward the centre of the object the pixel belongs to. Timeflows adds the same idea through time: per pixel of frame ``t``, where the centre of that object is in frame ``t+1``, and whether it has a successor at all (cells die, divide, leave the field). Linking objects between frames then reads the model instead of guessing from overlap, which is where the plain IoU stitcher fails: fast cells that move more than their own size between frames (the MuSC movies move 3-4 diameters per frame at p95).
records.translation: Cellpose predice, por píxel, un flujo hacia el centro del objeto al que pertenece el pixel. Los flujos de tiempo agregan la misma idea a través del tiempo: por pixEL del marco ``t``, donde el centro de ese objeto está en el marco =``t+1``, y si tiene un sucesor en absoluto (células mueren, dividen, dejan el campo de visión del microscopio). Vincular objetos entre marcos entonces lee el modelo en lugar de adivinar desde la superposición, que es donde falla la simple puntada de IoU: células rápidas que se mueven más que su propio tamaño entre marcos (las películas MuSC mueven 3-4 diámetros por marco en p95).

records.context: Centred on a random object of the first label image, jittered by up to a quarter window, so windows hold cells rather than empty background. A window shared by both frames leaves every displacement unchanged.
records.label: spacr.timeflows_model.random_window#1
records.source: Centred on a random object of the first label image, jittered by up to a quarter window, so windows hold cells rather than empty background. A window shared by both frames leaves every displacement unchanged.
records.translation: Centrado en un objeto aleatorio de la primera imagen de la etiqueta, movido por hasta un cuarto de ventana, por lo que las ventanas mantienen células en lugar de fondo vacío. Una ventana compartida por ambos marcos deja cada desplazamiento sin cambios.

records.context: The Cell Tracking Challenge publishes tracking ground truth as markers -- a small blob inside each cell, labelled with its track id in every frame -- and full outlines separately (the silver ``ST/SEG`` masks, labelled per frame). Only one-to-one assignments are retained: the object contains exactly one marker ID and that ID overlaps no other segmented object. Unmarked, merged and split assignments are excluded rather than guessed.
records.label: spacr.timeflows_model.track_masks_from_ctc#1
records.source: The Cell Tracking Challenge publishes tracking ground truth as markers -- a small blob inside each cell, labelled with its track id in every frame -- and full outlines separately (the silver ``ST/SEG`` masks, labelled per frame). Only one-to-one assignments are retained: the object contains exactly one marker ID and that ID overlaps no other segmented object. Unmarked, merged and split assignments are excluded rather than guessed.
records.translation: El Cell Tracking Challenge publica la verdad de la base de seguimiento como marcadores -- una pequeña mancha dentro de cada célula, etiquetada con su identificador de pista en cada marco -- y contornos completos por separado (las máscaras plateadas ``ST/SEG``, etiquetadas por marco). Sólo se retienen asignaciones individuales: el objeto contiene exactamente un ID de marcador y ese ID no se superpone con ningún otro objeto segmentado. Las asignaciones sin marcar, fusionadas y divididas se excluyen en lugar de adivinarse.

records.context: The timeflows plan rests on one claim about the training data: an object keeps the same label in every frame it appears in. A time-flow head is trained to point from a pixel of an object in frame ``t`` at that object's centre in frame ``t+1``, and the only thing that says which object in ``t+1`` is the same object is the label. If the annotation recycles a label after its object dies or leaves, the model is trained to point at an unrelated cell, and no later score catches it -- the held-out check scrambles the same wrong labels and agrees with itself.
records.label: spacr.timeflows_qc#2
records.source: The timeflows plan rests on one claim about the training data: an object keeps the same label in every frame it appears in. A time-flow head is trained to point from a pixel of an object in frame ``t`` at that object's centre in frame ``t+1``, and the only thing that says which object in ``t+1`` is the same object is the label. If the annotation recycles a label after its object dies or leaves, the model is trained to point at an unrelated cell, and no later score catches it -- the held-out check scrambles the same wrong labels and agrees with itself.
records.translation: El plan de flujos de tiempo se basa en una reclamación sobre los datos de entrenamiento: un objeto mantiene la misma etiqueta en cada marco en el que aparece. Se entrena un cabezal de flujo de tiempo para apuntar desde un píxel de un objeto en el marco ``t`` en el centro de ese objeto en marco =``t+1``, y lo único que dice qué objeto en ``t+1`` es el mismo objeto es la etiqueta. Si la anotación recicla una etiqueta después de que su objeto muere o se va, el modelo se entrena para apuntar en una célula no relacionada, y ninguna puntuación posterior lo atrapa; el cheque de retención revuelve las mismas etiquetas erróneas y está de acuerdo con sí mismo.

records.translation: **Runes de diferente longitud nunca están alineados.** Cada serie está trazada sobre su propio eje de época. Truncar una ejecución de 60 epoch para igualar a un vecino de 25 epoche inventa un resultado ("B never got better") y el relleno inventa una diferente; la leyenda muestra las longitudes de ejecución en su lugar.

records.source: **Train and validation are never silently mixed.** Every series label carries run, split and fold, and :func:`plot_curves` annotates the axes when more than one split is on it. records.translation: **El entrenamiento y la validación nunca se mezclan silenciosamente.** Cada etiqueta de la serie lleva ejecución, división y pliegue, y :func:`plot_curves` anota los ejes cuando hay más de una división en él. Una curva de entrenamiento por encima de una curva de validación es la definición de sobreajuste, no evidencia de que una ejecución le gane a otra.

records.source: Values the fit already holds are read, not recomputed. :func:`spacr.regression_diagnostics.design_report` answers the same questions, but it takes the well-by-guide matrix and pays for a fresh ``matrix_rank`` and a full SVD. A sweep does not have that matrix -- it has a fitted model -- and statsmodels computed the rank at fit time and kept it on ``model.model.rank``. Los nombres de campo de abajo coinciden deliberadamente con los de ``design_report`` para que los dos lean lo mismo en una carpeta de prueba.

records.context: optional separate folder for adjusted masks. None adjusts the cell masks in place. A separate folder keeps all source masks byte-identical, and every selected microscope field of view is rebuilt from its source on each invocation, including after interrupted work. In place, each adjusted mask's SHA-256 is recorded in :data:`ADJUSTED_CELLS_LEDGER` as it is written, and a mask whose bytes still match its record is skipped on the next run, because adjusting an adjusted mask merges it again and would change the result on every execute again. A cell mask segmented again no longer matches and is adjusted afresh.
records.label: spacr.utils.adjust_cell_masks#8
records.source: optional separate folder for adjusted masks. None adjusts the cell masks in place. A separate folder keeps all source masks byte-identical, and every selected field is rebuilt from its source on each invocation, including after interrupted work. In place, each adjusted mask's SHA-256 is recorded in :data:`ADJUSTED_CELLS_LEDGER` as it is written, and a mask whose bytes still match its record is skipped on the next run, because adjusting an adjusted mask merges it again and would change the result on every re-run. A cell mask segmented again no longer matches and is adjusted afresh.
records.translation: una carpeta separada opcional para máscaras ajustadas. None ajusta las máscaras celulares en su lugar. Una carpeta separada mantiene todas las máscaras fuente idénticas a byte, y cada campo de visión del microscopio seleccionado se reconstruye desde su fuente en cada invocación, incluyendo después de un trabajo interrumpido. En su lugar, la SHA-256 de cada máscara ajustada se registra en :data:`ADJUSTED_CELLS_LEDGER` tal como está escrita, y una mascara cuyos bytes todavía coinciden con su registro se salta en la siguiente ejecución, porque ajustar una máscara ajustada la fusiona de nuevo y cambiaría el resultado en cada ejecución de nuevo. Una mascatilla celular segmenta de nuevo ya no coincide y se ajusta de nuevo

records.context: All three frames are keyed on ``Feature`` and carry exactly one row per feature: ``rf_df`` is built from the feature list, and :func:`perform_statistical_tests` sends each feature to *either* ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis, never both. Hence ``validate='one_to_one'``: a repeated ``Feature`` -- from a frame with duplicated column names, or from two runs' results concatenated by mistake -- raises instead of multiplying the importance rows and reporting one feature several times.
records.label: spacr.utils.combine_results#1
records.source: All three frames are keyed on ``Feature`` and carry exactly one row per feature: ``rf_df`` is built from the feature list, and :func:`perform_statistical_tests` sends each feature to *either* ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis, never both. Hence ``validate='one_to_one'``: a repeated ``Feature`` -- from a frame with duplicated column names, or from two runs' results concatenated by mistake -- raises instead of multiplying the importance rows and reporting one feature several times.
records.translation: Los tres fotogramas están en ``Feature`` y llevan exactamente una fila por característica: ``rf_df`` se construye a partir de la lista de características, y :func:`perform_statistical_tests` envía cada característica a *o bien* ANOVA o Kruskal-Wallis, nunca ambos. Por lo tanto ``validate='one_to_one'``: un ``Feature`` repetido -- de un fotograma con nombres de columna duplicados, o de los resultados de dos ejecuciones concatenados por error -- aumenta en lugar de multiplicar las filas de importancia e informar de una característica varias veces.

records.context: Computing the position as ``sorted({nucleus, cell, pathogen, organelle})`` instead agrees with role order only when the roles are in ascending image data channel order. With ``nucleus_channel=2, cell_channel=0, organelle_channel=1`` the stack is ``[2, 0, 1]`` -- raw image data channel 1 sits at position 2 -- while the sorted reading gives position 1, which holds the cell image. Cellpose would then segment organelles on the cell image layer without any warning, and downstream counts and intensities would be measured from the wrong masks.
records.label: spacr.utils.dense_mask_channel_positions#2
records.source: Computing the position as ``sorted({nucleus, cell, pathogen, organelle})`` instead agrees with role order only when the roles are in ascending channel order. With ``nucleus_channel=2, cell_channel=0, organelle_channel=1`` the stack is ``[2, 0, 1]`` -- raw channel 1 sits at position 2 -- while the sorted reading gives position 1, which holds the cell image. Cellpose would then segment organelles on the cell plane without any warning, and downstream counts and intensities would be measured from the wrong masks.
records.translation: La computación de la posición como ``sorted({nucleus, cell, pathogen, organelle})`` en cambio está de acuerdo con el orden de rol sólo cuando los roles están en orden de canal de datos de imagen ascendente. Con ``nucleus_channel=2, cell_channel=0, organelle_channel=1`` la pila es ``[2, 0, 1]`` -- el canal de información de imagen en bruto 1 se encuentra en la posición 2 -- mientras que la lectura ordenada da la posición 1, que sostiene la imagen de la célula. Cellpose entonces segmentaría los orgánelos en la capa de imagen de célula sin ninguna advertencia, y los recuentos e intensidades posteriores se medirían a partir de las máscaras equivocadas.

records.source: General settings are inherited: axes, type, grid, legend, spines and the page come from :class:`spacr.style_base.FigureStyle`, so "font size" is one setting in spaCR rather than one per figure, and a house style saved on a volcano can be applied to any other figure that shares those names. records.translation: Los ajustes generales son heredados: ejes, tipo, cuadrícula, leyenda, espinas y la página provienen de :class:`spacr.style_base.FigureStyle`, por lo que "font size" es un ajuste en spaCR en lugar de uno por figura, y un estilo de casa guardado en un volcán se puede aplicar a cualquier otra figura que comparta esos nombres.
